final.memo:
We have held a substantial position in this institution since the crisis-era days when we provided preferred capital [D01], [D07]. The business remains a significant deposit-funded franchise, and we have long admired its role in the US banking system [D01]. However, maintaining an ownership stake above the 10% reporting threshold carries specific regulatory and administrative burdens that we find unnecessary to sustain at full scale [D08]. 

As we manage our capital allocation, we are mindful of the benefits of holding a larger cash position in an environment where many assets are fully priced [Rule S3]. Given our existing basis in these shares, a sale triggers a 21% federal tax charge [Rule S3], but we believe it is prudent to trim the position to improve liquidity and reduce the reporting complexity associated with our current ownership level [D08].

This decision is a matter of capital management and regulatory compliance rather than a fundamental change in our view of the company's long-term earning power [Rule S3]. We continue to regard the business as a solid, well-managed institution, and the remaining stake will continue to represent a significant investment for Berkshire [Rule S3]. We will proceed with the reduction in a measured fashion as we have with other major bank holdings in the past [Rule S3].
